Scch-24 1 M.V.C.659 of 2023

Before The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal
Court Of Small Causes, At Bengaluru.

(SCCH-24)
 Presided Over by Smt. Roopashri, B.Com., LL.B.,
 XXII ADDL., SCJ & ACJM,

. 
 Dated:- This the 4th day of October 2024  M.V.C. NO. 659 OF 2023 Petitioner/s:
1. Sri.Omkarappa N K S/o Kotturappa,
Aged about 57 years,
2. Smt. Shaila W/o Omakarappa N K Aged about 53 years,
3. Mamatha N O D/o Omkarappa N K W/o Sathisha P C Aged about 33 years,
All are R/at Niduvalli Villae & post,
Kadur Taluk,
Chikkamagaluru District.

(By Smt Usha Rani, Advocate)
 V/s  SCCH-24 2 M.V.C.659 of 2023 Respondents:
1. Mr.Bharath H S/o Hanumanthappa,
Street Anjaneya Layout,
Kurki, Davanagere -577514.

2 . New India Assurance Co.Ltd.,
Motor Claims HUB 3rd floor,
Mahalakshmi Chambers M.G road,
Omkarappa N.K vs Bharath.H on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190975377/
1 Bengaluru -560001.

(R-1 Exparte  R-2 by Sri.S.V Sudhakar Reddy, Adv.)
 JUDGMENT

This petition is filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with respect to the death of deceased Shivakumar N O who met with road traffic accident.
2. The petition averments in brief are that: On 26-12-2022 at about 08.30 p.m., the deceased was proceeding in his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-18-ED- 8841 on Panchanahalli- Belagur road.

When he reached near Niduvalli Lake at that time the lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16-D-0637 was parked in the middle of the road without taking proper precautions, prior indication, signal light and parking lights.

The deceased tried to steered his motorcycle, in the process the motorcycle touched the back right side of the lorry result of which the deceased fell down and sustained fatal injuries and died on the spot.

So far, the petitioners have spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies etc.,
3.
Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy.
The deceased was working as an agriculturist, taking tuition and working as a driver and earning sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the sudden demise of deceased, the petitioners have sustained mental and physical hardship.
Hence, respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
4. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 - Sri.Bharath H / R.C. owner of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16-D-0637 has remained absent.
Hence he was placed ex-parte.

5. The respondent No.2- the insurer of Lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-16-D-0637 has filed written statement and contended that the driver had parked the lorry on the correct side of the road as per the traffic Rules and regulations by putting parking lights on and driver had taken all precautionary measures and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry.

It is further contended that as per the records it is very clear that there was much space for the deceased to move his vehicle, but he drove his vehicle un-mindfully and negligently and he himself caused the accident, so the deceased himself is the tort- feasor.
It is further contended that the petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties.
The respondent no.2 has admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
It is further contended that the driver of the insured vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.

1. Whether the petitioners prove that, Sri.Shivakumar N O was died on account of road traffic accident on 26- 12-2022 at about 08-30 p.m., on Panchanahalli - Belaguru road, near Niduvalli lake,
Kadur Taluk,, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16-D-0637?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation ?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3.
What Order or Award?
7. In order to prove the case, 2nd petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and one witness is examined as Pw.2 and got marked in all 13 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13 and closed their side.
On the other hand, the respondent no.2 has examined its Assistant as Rw.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.R1 to Ex.R3.

8. Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioners and respondent no.2 and perused the entire materials placed on record.
9.

My findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue no 2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following;
REASONS 10. Issue No.1 :- Petitioners have categorically contended that on the date of accident, the deceased was proceeding in his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 18-ED-8841 on Panchanahalli- Belagur road.
When he reached near Niduvalli Lake at that time the lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16-D-0637 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) was parked in the middle of the road without taking proper precaution, prior indication, signal light and parking lights.

The deceased tried to steer his motorcycle, in the process the motorcycle touched the back right side of the lorry result of which the deceased fell down and sustained fatal injuries and died on the spot.
11. In order to substantiate the petition averments, the petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW1.
In the examination in chief, she has reiterated the petition averments.

In support of the contention,
he has produced 8 documents which are at Ex.P1 to Ex.P8 i.e., F.I.R with complaint, Inquest report with statement, crime details form, 133 notice, 133 notice reply, IMV report, PM report and charge sheet
are the material documents to prove the present issue.

12. On the basis of the complaint lodged by N K Onkarappa who is the father of deceased, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No 0056/2022 of Panchanahalli Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279, 304 (A) of IPC.
The Investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 304(A) of IPC.

Omkarappa N.K vs Bharath.H on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190975377/
3 13.

So far as the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of offending vehicle is concerned, it is not in dispute that the accident in question has occurred on the stated date at about 8-30 p.m.,
i.e., in the night hour.
The accident in question has occurred in Panchanahalli -Belagur road.
The deceased was proceeding from Panchanahalli towards Belagur.
If the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, the width of the road at the spot of accident is nearly 18 feet.
The offending vehicle was parked in the said road by encroaching nearly 6 feet road.
In the said road vehicles from both direction is flying.

It was much argued by the learned counsel for respondent no.2 that there was much space remained on the right side of Panachanahalli - Belagur road and deceased could have passed through the right side of the offending vehicle and if deceased had passed through the right side of the road this accident could have been avoided.
It was also argued that the offending vehicle was stationed on the left side of the road by taking all precautionary measures i.e., by putting indication and signal.

14. If entire police records is perused, there is no whisper in the documents and evidence regarding the precautionary measures taken by the driver of the offending vehicle while parking the offending vehicle in the night hours that too in the middle of the road.
As observed supra it was night hour and offending vehicle was stationed in the road without any signal.
Under such circumstances one cannot anticipate the vehicle stationed in the road.
When deceased was riding the two wheeler, he has rightly ridden his vehicle on the left side of the road.
Had the deceased noticed the stationed offending vehicle at a little distance, he could have taken his vehicle on the right side of the road.

Hence, at first the driver of the offending vehicle ought not to have stationed his vehicle in the middle of the road and secondly while parking the vehicle in the road that too in night hours he ought to have taken all precautionary measures by giving proper indication to the other vehicle user passing in the said road.

At the cost of repetition though the respondent no.2 has contended that the driver has parked the vehicle by taking all precautionary measures but they have failed to prove the same by not examining the driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence, there is no material placed on record by the respondent no.2 to substantiate their defence.
Hence materials placed on record clearly proves the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of offending vehicle.
Hence this court holds issue no 1 in the Affirmative.

15. Issue No.2:- It is the contention taken by the petitioners that, petitioner No.1 and 2 being the parents and petitioner no.3 being the sister of the deceased are entirely depending on the earnings of the deceased and that deceased was working as an agriculturist, taking tuition and working as a part time driver and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m.
16.

One can not dispute that petitioners no 1 and 2 being the parents of the deceased are the dependents of the deceased but petitioner no 3 being the married sister of the deceased is not the dependent of the deceased .
17.
It is stated by the petitioners that at the time of accident the deceased was aged about 31 years.
The petitioners have produced Aadhar card of the deceased which reflects the date of birth of deceased as 13-08-1991.
Hence as on the date of accident the deceased was aged about 31 years.

Omkarappa N.K vs Bharath.H on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190975377/
4 18.

As it is observed earlier, it is contended by the petitioners that deceased was working as an agriculturist, taking tuition and working as a part time driver and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/-
p.m.
The petitioners have produced BE marks card and ID card of the deceased as per Ex.P12.
So far as the income of the deceased, in order to prove the same petitioners have not produced any materials.

Hence taking in to consideration the age of the deceased and the year in which accident in question had occurred, this court inclines to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.15,500/-
p.m.
19.

Keeping in mind the observation made in Sarala Verma's case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298,
considering the family status of the deceased as he was bachelor 50% of annual income is to be deducted towards the personal expenses and remaining 50% is to be considered for assessing the compensation under the head loss of dependency.

20. Regarding loss of future prospects, in a ruling reported in 2018 (2) CCC 233 (SC) Munuswamy and Ors/Managing Director Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd) it was held that while computation of compensation, future prospect of deceased is to be considered by addition to be made to actual income of the deceased which existed at the time of his death.

entities.text: Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd)
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is further observed that in case the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary an addition of 40% of the established income should be warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years, An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.

Hence in the instant case as the victim was 31 years the addition towards future prospect should be 40%.
21.
Now by assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.15,500/- of which 40% is added towards future prospect which comes to Rs.21,700/-.
Out of it if 50% is deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased it comes around Rs.10,850/-.
The appropriate multiplier applicable is 16 for the age of the deceased.
Accordingly the petitioner is entitled towards loss of dependency at Rs.20,83,200/- (10,850x 12 x 16).
22. Because of the untimely death of deceased, the petitioner's no1 and 2 have lost their son and petitioner no.3 lost her brother thereby lost the love and affection of deceased.

So far as the quantum of compensation awarded under the head loss of consortium, towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses is concerned slab has been fixed in Pranay Sethi's case reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

In para 61 of the said judgment the reasonable figures on conventional heads namely loss of estate, loss of consortium, and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/, Rs.40,000/-
and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
It is further observed that the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

The judgment in Pranay Sethi's case was rendered on 30th October 2017.
23.

As per the observation made in Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd, the Hon'ble Supreme court awarded spousal consortium for wife,
parental consortium and filial consortium.

entities.text: Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This was the terms of the judgment in National Omkarappa N.K vs Bharath.H on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190975377/
5

entities.text: National Omkarappa N.K vs Bharath.H on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Insurance Company Ltd / Pranay Sethi and Ors.

By applying the observation made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years has lapsed from the date of order amount of consortium fixed in Pranay Sethi's Case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.

Though petitioner no 3 is not the dependent of the deceased but she being the sister of deceased she is also entitled for compensation of Rs 48,400 under the head filial consortium Hence, this court deems it appropriate to award compensation of Rs.48,400/- each to the petitioners under the head loss of filial consortium.

Petitioners are further entitled for funeral expenses to the tune of Rs.18,150/- and Rs.18,150/-
towards loss of estate.

24. In the circumstances, the loss assessed by the petitioners due to the death of deceased is calculated as follows:
 SL Heads Amount  1 Transportation and Rs. 18,150/-
Funeral
Expenses

2 Loss of estate Rs. 18,150/-
 3. Loss of spousal Rs.1,45,200/-
 consortium, parental  consortium and filial  consortium  (Rs.48,400x3)
 4. Loss of Dependency Rs.20,83,200/-

Thus, in all petitioner is entitled to Rs.22,64,700/- (Rupees Twenty Two Lakh Sixty Four thousand Seven Hundred only) and it is just and adequate compensation under the facts and circumstances of the case.
25. As regarding liability is concerned, in view of the finding on issue No.2 there is liability on the part of the insurer of offending vehicle to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
The compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6 % per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
In the result Issue No.3 is answered partly in the Affirmative.
26. Issue No.4:
In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 to 3 , my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioners is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.22,64,700 + cost of Rs.1000/- imposed vide order date 16-12- 2023.
In all the petitioners are entitled for sum of Rs.22,65,700/- (Rupees Twenty Two Lakh Sixty Five Thousand Seven Hundred only).
Sum of Rs.22,64,700/- shall carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

Omkarappa N.K vs Bharath.H on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190975377/
6
The Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the amount along with interest within two months from the date of award.
Petitioner no1 is entitled for Rs.8,00,000/- Petitioner no 2 is entitled for Rs.14,17,300/-

Petitioner no 3 is entitled for Rs.48,400/-
Out of the compensation awarded and interest to the petitioner no1 and 2, 50% shall be deposited in their name in any nationalized bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50%
shall be released to the petitioners No.1 and 2 on proper identification.
Entire compensation amount awarded in favour of petitioner No.3 shall be released to petitioner through E-payment on proper identification Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
